mainTopic: How the meat of a קרבן gets הכשר, why stomach secretions stay pure, and how levels of טומאה are counted from a שרץ
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier answer. A vessel lying on the ground counts as 'something that can be asked' about, so the knife found in the עזרה is pure only because the עזרה is treated as a רשות הרבים. The גמרא then asks how the meat of a קרבן could become טמא at all, since food needs a liquid to give it הכשר first. Blood of קדשים, the liquids of the slaughter area, and חיבת הקודש are each suggested and pushed back. Then רב יהודה in the name of שמואל answers that the cow was still wet from a river. Next the גמרא explains why stomach secretions (פרש) do not make the meat טמא. רב אדא בר אהבה says they were thick, and רב אשי says they are a foul liquid. A ברייתא about a chain of טומאה from a שרץ is then corrected so that it counts three levels, with the brewing vat as a memory aid. Finally, רב אדא בר אהבה asks why bread in an oven with a שרץ is only שני. רבא begins to answer from a ברייתא, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even an object on the ground counts as 'able to be asked about'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. A vessel lying on the ground is treated like something that has understanding to be asked, because people will ask a חכם about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: People ask a Sage about it, so even a vessel resting on the ground is treated like something that has understanding to be asked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started earlier. It explains why the knife's purity had to depend on the עזרה being a רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a ספק טומאה in a private domain is טמא applies only to 'something that has understanding to be asked' (דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל). You might think a knife is excluded, since a knife cannot answer questions. The גמרא says no: its owners will bring the question to a חכם, so even an object on the ground falls under this rule. That is why the only reason the knife is pure is that the עזרה counts as a רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: They ask (a Sage) about it
A vessel resting on the ground
Something that has understanding to be asked; the condition for treating a ספק טומאה in a private domain as טמא

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the knife can actually think. It means the law treats the case as if it could be asked about, because a person will ask on its behalf.
steps.whatToRemember: The knife is pure only because the עזרה is treated as a רשות הרבים. Being an inanimate object on the ground would not have been enough to make it pure.

phrases.english: They ask (a Sage) about it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּכְלִי הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע —
phrases.english: even a vessel that is resting on the ground
is like something that has understanding to be asked.
phrases.notes: So the rule of ספק טומאה ברשות היחיד can apply to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁאָלִין עָלֶיהָ, אֲפִילּוּ בִּכְלִי הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening a category: an inanimate object on the ground is included in דבר שיש בו דעת לישאל because people ask about it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A knife cannot be asked anything, so it should be pure no matter which domain it is in.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because people will ask about it, it is treated like it can be asked. So its purity rests only on the עזרה being a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: With what liquid was the meat made ready for impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'the meat is impure' and asks which liquid gave this meat הכשר, which it needs before it can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the meat is impure.' This meat, with what was it made ready to become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the source quoted on the previous amud, the ruling that the meat is impure. It asks how that is even possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after it has been made wet by one of the special liquids. This step is called הכשר. A freshly slaughtered קרבן seems not to have touched any qualifying liquid yet. So the גמרא asks which liquid did the job, and the next steps try out possible answers.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the meat is impure', the words of the source (quoted on the previous amud) being discussed
Was made ready (got הכשר) to receive טומאה
With what?

steps.whyThisMatters: This question sets up the whole next section. Each answer the גמרא suggests will have to get past the special rules about liquids in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: "And the meat is impure."
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא about a needle found in the flesh of an offering.

phrases.english: This meat, with what was it made susceptible (to impurity)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the knife to the meat, a different clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which liquid made the קרבן meat ready to receive טומאה.

steps.title: The blood cannot be the liquid, because blood of offerings does not make food ready
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the animal's blood made the meat ready. It rejects this using רבי יוחנן's teaching that דם קדשים does not give הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was made ready by the blood, didn't רבי חייא בר אבא say in the name of רבי יוחנן: How do we know that blood of offerings does not make food ready? Because the verse says, 'Do not eat it; pour it on the ground like water.' Blood that is poured out like water makes food ready. Blood that is not poured out like water does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer: the blood from the שחיטה made the meat ready. It immediately knocks this down using a teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from an ordinary animal (חולין) is poured onto the ground, so the פסוק compares it to water, and it can give הכשר. Blood of קדשים is collected in a vessel and brought to the מזבח, so it is not 'poured like water'. That blood cannot make food ready, so it cannot explain why this meat is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of consecrated offerings
Makes food ready (gives הכשר) to receive טומאה
'You shall pour it like water'; the source that blood can count as a liquid for הכשר
'But didn't [so-and-so] say?' A formula used to push back with a known teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with whether the blood is pure or impure. The question here is only whether the blood can make other food ready to become impure.

phrases.english: If we say that it was made susceptible by the blood,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that blood of offerings does not make susceptible?
As it is said: "You shall not eat it;
upon the ground you shall pour it like water" (Devarim 12:16).
Blood that is poured out like water makes susceptible,
and blood that is not poured out like water does not make susceptible.
phrases.notes: This is blood of קדשים, which is collected for the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא דְּאִיתַּכְשַׁר בְּדָם, וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 2 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out blood as the liquid that gave this meat הכשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By a דרשה of רבי יוחנן, blood of קדשים is not 'poured like water', so it cannot give הכשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the blood made the meat ready
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that blood of קדשים is not a liquid that gives הכשר.

steps.title: The slaughter-area liquids cannot be the answer either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the liquids of the Temple slaughter area made the meat ready. It rejects this because רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says those liquids do not give הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it was made ready by the liquids of the slaughterhouse. But didn't רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא say: The liquids of the slaughterhouse are not only pure, they also do not make food ready!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer: the water and other liquids in the Temple slaughter area made the meat ready. This answer is rejected too. Step 5 tries another idea, and step 7 gives the accepted answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that משקי בית מטבחיא are pure is already known. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא adds a further point: they do not even give הכשר. So they cannot explain why the meat became טמא, and the גמרא keeps looking. Step 7 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The liquids of the Temple slaughter area (water and blood near the מזבח)
Pure (Aramaic)
'It is not enough that…'; introduces an even bigger point
'Rather…'; introduces a new attempt after the first one failed

steps.whatToRemember: Two possible liquids, the blood and the slaughter-area liquids, have both been ruled out. Step 5 tries חיבת הקודש next, and step 7 gives the answer that is accepted: river water still on the animal.

phrases.english: Rather, say that it was made susceptible
by the liquids of the slaughterhouse.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, say:
The liquids of the slaughterhouse:
not only are they pure,
phrases.notes: Based on the testimony of יוסי בן יועזר.

phrases.english: but they also do not make (food) susceptible!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the blood suggestion fails, the גמרא tries a second answer and rejects it as well.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the slaughter-area liquids as the source of הכשר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that these liquids do not give הכשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that משקי בית מטבחיא made the meat ready
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling of an אמורא says these liquids cannot make food ready, not just that they are pure.

steps.title: Suggestion that holiness itself made the meat ready, and its rejection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that חיבת הקודש made the meat ready for טומאה. It rejects this because חיבת הקודש may only make the meat itself פסול. It may not be strong enough to count ראשון and שני, meaning to pass טומאה on further.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the meat became ready through the special love for holy things. But even if that love makes the meat itself disqualified, does it also let us count first-level and second-level impurity from it?!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third attempt to explain how the meat became ready for טומאה. The גמרא suggests that its holiness alone did it, and then questions that idea right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חיבת הקודש means that holy food is so precious that the חכמים treat it as able to become טמא even without contact with a liquid. But the ruling 'the meat is טמא' gives the meat a real level in the regular chain of ראשון and שני, as something that could pass טומאה further. It is not just a disqualification of the meat itself. It is not clear that חיבת הקודש is strong enough to do that.

keyTerms.meaning: The special love for holy things. Because of it, holy food can become טמא even without the usual liquid הכשר.
To make the item itself פסול, without passing טומאה on to anything else
First-level and second-level טומאה, the chain of passing impurity along
"Say" or "granted". It introduces a limit on the suggestion.

steps.confusionAlert: Making something itself פסול is not the same as making it able to pass טומאה on to other things. The rejection depends on this difference.

phrases.english: Rather, that it was made ready (for impurity)
through the special love for holy things.
Say that the love for holy things works for it
to disqualify the meat itself,
does it also let us count first and second levels from it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After blood and Temple liquids were rejected, this is a third suggestion for the source of the הכשר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חיבת הקודש as the explanation for our case, where the meat is treated as fully טמא within the chain of ראשון and שני.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חיבת הקודש may only make the item itself פסול. It may not create a chain of ראשון and שני.

steps.title: If holiness were enough, ריש לקיש's open question would already be answered
steps.stepSummary: If our case proved that חיבת הקודש allows counting ראשון and שני, it would answer ריש לקיש's question about a lump of מנחה. Since that question remains open, we cannot assume it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, solve the question that ריש לקיש asked: with a lump of flour from מנחות, do we count first and second levels of impurity from it or not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens the rejection from the last step. It points out that this exact issue is a famous unsolved question of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צריד of מנחות can only become טמא because of חיבת הקודש, so it matches our case exactly. ריש לקיש was unsure whether it passes טומאה along. Our משנה cannot be explained by something ריש לקיש himself left as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: "Resolve!": then this would answer an open question
A dry lump or clump of flour
Flour offerings
An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Then resolve what Reish Lakish asked:
a dry lump of meal-offerings,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנִין בּוֹ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי אוֹ לֹא!
phrases.english: do we count first and second levels from it or not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection in step 5 by tying it to an open question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Completes the rejection of the חיבת הקודש explanation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would settle ריש לקיש's question, which is left open.

steps.title: שמואל's case: the animal was still wet from the river
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that the animal was a שלמים cow. It was led through a river and slaughtered while still wet. That water gave the meat its הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for example, it was a cow brought as a שלמים offering. The owner led it through a river and slaughtered it while liquid was still moist on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally gives a working answer to the question of how the meat became ready for טומאה. It was ordinary river water still on the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood and Temple liquids do not give הכשר, and חיבת הקודש is uncertain. So שמואל points to a normal liquid, water, that gives הכשר for sure. Water that is טופח, wet enough to wet something else, can wet the meat during skinning.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, whose hide and meat go to the owner
He led it through a river
Liquid wet enough to make something else wet

steps.whatToRemember: The meat in the needle case became ready for טומאה through river water still on the animal, not through blood, Temple liquids, or חיבת הקודש.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For example, where it was a cow
of peace-offerings,
and he led it through a river and slaughtered it,
while moist liquid was still on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיְתָה פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2 after three suggestions failed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case (אוקימתא) to include an ordinary liquid
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the meat had no clear source of הכשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: River water still on the animal made the meat ready.

steps.title: Why don't the stomach secretions make the meat impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the needle was found in the פרש, everything is טהור. It asks why the liquid פרש does not itself become טמא and pass it back to the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the needle was found in the stomach secretions, everything is pure. But let the secretions turn around and make the meat impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids that touch טומאה become ראשון לטומאה by rabbinic law, and they can make food טמא. The פרש touched the impure needle, so it should become טמא and then make the meat טמא. Why, then, does the משנה say everything is טהור?

keyTerms.meaning: The contents or secretions in an animal's stomach
"Let it turn around" and pass the טומאה back
It was found

phrases.english: If it was found in the stomach secretions —
everything is pure.
But let the secretions turn around
and make the meat impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that everything is טהור when the needle is found in the פרש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The liquid פרש should become טמא from the needle and then make the meat טמא.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the secretions were thick
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the משנה is talking about thick פרש. Thick פרש is not a liquid, so it does not pass on טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: the case is thick secretions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the question by saying the פרש was solid, not liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special rule that liquids become ראשון only applies to real liquids. Thick פרש counts as a solid, so it does not pick up and pass on טומאה that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick or solid
An אמורא

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It is referring to thick secretions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: בְּפֶרֶשׁ עָבָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the פרש was liquid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרש was thick, so it is not a liquid that passes on טומאה.

steps.title: רב אשי: even soft secretions are a spoiled liquid
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even soft פרש does not make the meat טמא. It is a spoiled, foul liquid, and such a liquid does not pass on טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: you can even say it is soft secretions, because it is a foul liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second, broader answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not need the case to be thick פרש. He says a foul liquid is not considered a real liquid for טומאה. So even runny פרש stays harmless.

keyTerms.meaning: Soft or runny
A spoiled, foul liquid that does not count as a liquid for טומאה
"You can even say". It introduces a broader answer.

steps.whatToRemember: The פרש does not make the meat טמא. רב אדא בר אהבה says this is because it was thick. רב אשי says it is because even soft פרש is a foul liquid.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it is soft secretions,
because it is a foul liquid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּפֶרֶשׁ רַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רב אדא בר אהבה to the same קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a legal reason that applies to all cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Soft פרש would count as a real liquid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A foul liquid does not pass on טומאה, so even soft פרש leaves everything טהור.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists a chain of טומאה starting from a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב ששת. It describes a chain: שרץ makes liquids טמא, liquids make a vessel טמא, the vessel makes foods טמא, and foods make liquids טמא. It concludes that we learn three levels of טומאה from a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught before רב ששת: A שרץ makes liquids טמא. Liquids make a vessel טמא. A vessel makes foods טמא. Foods make liquids טמא. So we have learned three levels of טומאה that come from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out a chain of טומאה passing from one item to the next, starting with a שרץ. It ends by saying this teaches three levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the ברייתא is to show how far טומאה travels from a שרץ according to the Torah. Each link in the chain is a new level: ראשון, then שני, then שלישי. Pay close attention to the count, because the next step will question it.

keyTerms.meaning: The reciter taught (a person who memorized and recited ברייתות in the study hall)
A dead creeping creature; an אב הטומאה
Liquids
A vessel or utensil
Foods

phrases.english: The reciter taught before Rav Sheshet:
A creeping creature makes liquids impure,
and liquids make the vessel impure,
and the vessel makes the foods impure,
and the foods make the liquids impure.
And we have learned three levels of impurity from a creeping creature.
phrases.notes: The count of 'three' is what the next step challenges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the needle-and-פרש discussion to a ברייתא about how many levels of טומאה come from a שרץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From a שרץ, the Torah teaches three successive levels of טומאה, passing through vessel, food, and liquid.

steps.title: The chain lists four, not three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא actually lists four links after the שרץ, yet it says 'three'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts the links in the ברייתא and finds four (liquids, vessel, foods, liquids). That doesn't match the ברייתא's own conclusion of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about the wording of the ברייתא. The steps listed and the number stated contradict each other, so something in the text needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: These are four!

phrases.english: These are four!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count stated at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists four links of טומאה after the שרץ, so the number 'three' does not fit.

steps.title: Remove the first 'liquids'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we should cut out the liquids at the beginning of the chain. Then the chain reads: שרץ makes a vessel טמא, the vessel makes food טמא, and the food makes liquid טמא. That is three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cut out the liquids of the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא by removing the first link, 'שרץ makes liquids טמא, and liquids make a vessel טמא'. Now the שרץ goes straight to the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the cut, the chain is: vessel (ראשון), food (שני), liquid (שלישי). That gives exactly three levels, matching the ברייתא's conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut out (remove from the text)
The first part of a teaching

phrases.english: Cut out the liquids of the first clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counting problem by changing the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as written lists four links.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first 'liquids' should be removed, so the שרץ makes the vessel טמא directly, giving three levels.

steps.title: Why not remove the last 'liquids' instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we cut the first liquids. We could just as easily cut the liquids at the end ('foods make liquids טמא') and still get three.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, cut out the liquids of the last part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fix. There are two 'liquids' in the chain, so why pick the first one to remove?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either cut brings the count down to three. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing the first cut over the last one.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite makes more sense
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: On the contrary, cut out the liquids of the latter clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the specific emendation chosen in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to remove the first 'liquids'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing the last 'liquids' would also produce three levels, so the first choice needs a reason.

steps.title: Liquids making a vessel טמא is a rejected view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the only תנא who says liquids make a vessel טמא is רבי יהודה, and he took it back. So the link 'liquids make a vessel טמא' must be the one removed. A memory aid is given: a brewing vat (נזייתא).
steps.simpleTranslation: We don't find any תנא who says 'liquids make a vessel טמא' except רבי יהודה, and he retracted. Your memory sign is: a brewing vat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for cutting the first liquids. The idea that liquids make a vessel טמא (by Torah law) was held only by רבי יהודה, and he changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last link, 'foods make liquids טמא', is accepted law. The first link depends on liquids making a vessel טמא, which nobody holds in the end. So the first link goes. The mnemonic נזייתא reminds you of the correct order: in a brewing vat you have the vessel, then the grain (food), then the water (liquid). That is vessel → food → liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found
He retracted (changed his mind)
Your mnemonic (memory sign)
A brewing vat used for making beer

steps.whatToRemember: The fixed ברייתא reads: שרץ → vessel (ראשון) → food (שני) → liquid (שלישי). Liquids making a vessel טמא is not Torah law, because רבי יהודה retracted. Remember it by the brewing vat: vessel, grain, water.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that liquids never make a vessel טמא at all. The point here is only that this is not Torah law, so it can't be a link in a chain that counts Torah-level steps.

phrases.english: We have not found a tanna who says
'liquids make a vessel impure'
except Rabbi Yehuda, and he retracted it.
And your mnemonic is: a brewing vat.
phrases.notes: In a vat you place the vessel, then the grain, then the water, the same order as the chain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר מַשְׁקִין מְטַמְּאִין כְּלִי אֶלָּא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the emendation of step 13 against the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grounding the textual choice in the accepted halacha
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either 'liquids' could be cut equally well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the first link depends on liquids making a vessel טמא, a view that was retracted, so it must be the one removed.

steps.title: A משנה: bread in an oven with a שרץ is שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere. If a שרץ is found in an oven, the bread inside is only שני, because the oven itself is ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: If a שרץ is found in an oven, the bread inside it is שני, because the oven is ראשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about an oven made טמא by a שרץ. It is setting up a question that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שרץ makes the oven ראשון, and the oven in turn makes the bread שני. The bread is treated as touching the oven, not the שרץ itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
An oven (an earthenware vessel)
Second-level טומאה (שני)
First-level טומאה (ראשון)

phrases.english: We learned there: A creeping creature that was found in an oven —
the bread inside it is second-level,
because the oven is first-level.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about levels of טומאה, this time inside an oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שרץ in an oven makes the oven ראשון, and bread inside the oven is שני.

steps.title: Why not treat the oven as full of טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks רבא: an earthenware oven becomes טמא through its airspace, so why not treat the whole oven as if it were filled with טומאה? Then the bread would be like it touched the שרץ and should be ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: Let us view this oven as if it were full of טומאה, and this bread should be ראשון!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges the משנה's ruling that the bread is only שני. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earthenware vessel becomes טמא when a שרץ is in its airspace, even without any touching. רב אדא suggests that this means the whole inside of the oven counts as 'filled' with the שרץ's טומאה. If so, the bread sitting inside is like it touched the שרץ directly and should be ראשון, not שני.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us view (consider) it
It is like something filled with טומאה
First-level (ראשון)

steps.confusionAlert: The bread did not touch the שרץ. The question is only whether the oven's airspace should count as if it were full of the שרץ.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
And let us view this oven
as if it is like something filled with impurity,
and this bread should be first-level!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא: וְנִיחְזֵי לְהַאי תַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the bread in the oven is only שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earthenware oven becomes טמא through its airspace, so it should count as filled with טומאה. That would make the bread inside like something touching the שרץ itself, which is ראשון.

steps.title: רבא rejects the idea and begins quoting a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב אדא בר אהבה that the oven is not treated as if it were filled with טומאה. He begins citing a ברייתא as proof. The ברייתא opens with a possibility it will later reject: maybe all vessels become טמא from the airspace of a כלי חרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You cannot think that. A ברייתא teaches: 'One might have thought that all vessels become טמא from the airspace of an earthenware vessel.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 17 with a firm 'no' and starts quoting a ברייתא to prove it. This step only sets up the proof, because the ברייתא's actual conclusion comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה wanted to treat the oven's airspace as if it were packed with טומאה. If that were true, anything inside would count as touching the שרץ directly. The ברייתא tests this idea by asking whether every kind of vessel inside would then become טמא. That outcome is clearly not the הלכה, as the rest of the ברייתא will show, so the airspace cannot really be treated as 'full of טומאה.'

keyTerms.meaning: "It cannot enter your mind": a strong rejection of a suggestion
"As it was taught": introduces a ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)
"One might have thought": opens a possibility that the ברייתא will later reject
The airspace (inside) of an earthenware vessel, through which it becomes טמא and passes on טומאה
Become טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The line 'all vessels become טמא from the airspace' is NOT the ברייתא's conclusion. The word יכול means 'you might have thought this,' and the ברייתא is about to reject it. Do not take it as the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit on what airspace טומאה can do. A כלי חרס's airspace passes טומאה only in specific ways. It is not the same as the item inside physically touching the source of טומאה, and that is why the bread in the oven stays שני.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: This cannot enter your mind,
phrases.notes: רבא is responding to רב אדא בר אהבה's question from Step 17.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: Introduces the source רבא will use as proof.

phrases.english: One might have thought that all the vessels
phrases.notes: The 'might have thought' setup, which will be rejected.

phrases.english: become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel —
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud with its rejection and derivation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of רב אדא בר אהבה in Step 17 by rejecting its premise and starting a proof from a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise of the question, backed by a source of the תנאים (ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oven's airspace should be treated as if it were filled with טומאה, so the bread inside would count as touching the שרץ and be ראשון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Airspace טומאה does not equal being filled with טומאה. The ברייתא, once completed, shows that not everything inside a טמא כלי חרס becomes טמא from its airspace, so the bread stays שני.
